neighbours.label: position predicting a speech verb: what someone was [saying], the words they should [be saying]
fire: He heard voices but couldn't make out what they were saying.
Through the wall I could hardly understand what she was saying.
The coach whispered the words the actor should be saying.
Nobody in the back could hear what the speaker was saying.
I nodded politely, but I had no idea what he was saying.
The noise was so loud we couldn't tell what they were shouting.
She leaned closer to catch what the old man was saying.
We only shared names because we couldn't say much more.
quiet: He heard voices but couldn't make out where they were going.
Through the wall I could hardly understand why she was angry.
The coach showed the actor where he should be standing.
Nobody in the back could see what the speaker was holding.
I nodded politely, but I had no idea where he was from.
The noise was so loud we couldn't sleep that night.
She leaned closer to see what the old man was reading.
We only shared a table because the cafe was full.
